What are you going to order?
Today I want to eat something with broth.
-고 싶어요 (go sipeoyo) = want to: 먹고 싶어요 = want to eat.
The weather is really nice today.
비가 와요 (biga wayo) = 'rain comes' — how Korean says it's raining.
Yesterday it rained all day long.
하루 종일 (haru jongil) = all day long.
The weather is too hot these days.
Last night it was a bit cold.
바람이 불어요 (barami bureoyo) = the wind blows.
눈 (nun) = snow AND eye — context decides!
Last winter it snowed a lot.
The monsoon season has already started.
장마 (jangma) = summer monsoon rains — guaranteed June small talk.
The fine dust is bad today.
미세먼지 (misemeonji) = fine-dust pollution — Koreans check it like weather.
In the afternoon the sky was clear.
맑아요 (malgayo) = is clear — for skies and water.
The weather will be nice this weekend.
In spring lots of flowers bloom.
In winter the house is a bit cold.
On weekends I rest at home.
On Saturdays I sleep in late.
I took a nap on the sofa.
낮잠 (natjam) = daytime nap: 낮잠을 자요 = take a nap.
On Sundays I do nothing at all.
This weekend I'm going to rest up.
푹 쉬어요 (puk swieoyo) = rest deeply — wished to every tired friend.
I watched two movies at home.
편 (pyeon) counts movies and shows: 두 편 (du pyeon = two films).
내내 (naenae) = all through: 주말 내내 = the whole weekend.
I went to the Han River park with a friend.
한강 (Hangang) = Seoul's river — picnics, bikes, and chicken.
Did you rest well over the weekend?
Monday-morning Korean: 잘 쉬었어요? (jal swieosseoyo? = did you rest well?)
What are you doing next weekend?
I sent a text to my friend.
문자 (munja) = text message: 문자를 보내요 = send a text.
Did you see my KakaoTalk message?
카톡 (katok) = KakaoTalk — Korea's do-everything messaging app.
I sent the photos over KakaoTalk.
답장 (dapjang) = a reply to a message.
배터리가 없어요 (baeteoriga eopseoyo) = 'no battery' = my phone's dying.
I left my phone at home.
놓고 왔어요 (noko wasseoyo) = left it behind — the forgot-it phrase.
I KakaoTalk with my family every day.
Add 하다 to anything: 카톡해요 (katokaeyo) = to message on KakaoTalk.
바꿔요 (bakkwoyo) = change (something): 번호를 바꿔요 = change a number.
I bought a new phone last week.
I took lots of photos at the Han River.
사진을 찍어요 (sajineul jjigeoyo) = take a photo.
I took a selfie with my friend.
써요 (sseoyo) = use AND write — one verb, two jobs.
I don't look at my phone at night.
I set the alarm for six thirty.
알람을 맞춰요 (allameul matchwoyo) = set an alarm.
I make the bed every morning.
이불 (ibul) = blanket/bedding — you 'tidy' it, not 'make' it.
The cat sleeps on the sofa.
I walk the dog every morning.
I made ramyeon in the evening.
끓여요 (kkeuryeoyo) = boil up: 라면을 끓여요 = make ramyeon.
I baked bread at home over the weekend.
On Sunday mornings we have brunch.
I planted new flowers in the balcony pots.
심어요 (simeoyo) = plant: 꽃을 심어요 = plant flowers.
There are family photos on the wall.
Our home is the best place in the world.
제일 (jeil) = the most: 제일 좋아요 = like it best.
